original_question: Is the class of lattices that are isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of subgroups of some Abelian group self-dual?
target_in_paper: Section 2 ("Problems of 2025"), Problem 39: "Is the class of lattices that are isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of subgroups of some Abelian group self-dual?"
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact open problem stated in the paper: the representation class is lattices embeddable as sublattices of subgroup lattices of Abelian groups, and the property under discussion is self-duality of that class.
missing_details: Spell out what "self-dual" means in quantifier form: if a lattice L is isomorphic to a sublattice of Sub(A) for some Abelian group A, must the dual lattice L^op also be isomorphic to a sublattice of Sub(B) for some Abelian group B?
Specify that "the lattice of subgroups" means the full subgroup lattice Sub(A), ordered by inclusion.
Make explicit that the objects are abstract lattices and that the representation is lattice-theoretic: an isomorphism onto a sublattice preserving finite meets and joins.
Do not add any extra hypotheses such as finiteness, modularity, distributivity, or restrictions on the Abelian group; the paper states none.
refined_question: Let L be an abstract lattice. Suppose there exists an Abelian group A such that L is isomorphic to a sublattice of the subgroup lattice Sub(A), ordered by inclusion. Must the dual lattice L^op also be isomorphic to a sublattice of Sub(B) for some Abelian group B?
justification: The draft is already essentially verbatim the paper’s official formulation: in the notebook it appears as Problem 39 in the 2025 problems list. The surrounding items show that this is part of a cluster of representability questions for lattices embeddable into subgroup, normal-subgroup, and subspace lattices, but Problem 39 itself is stated without any additional finiteness or structural assumptions. Therefore the only paper-faithful sharpening is to unpack the standard phrase "self-dual" into the explicit dual-embeddability question and to name the subgroup lattice as Sub(A) ordered by inclusion. Any further restriction would go beyond the paper’s actual statement.
